steps.title: Final editing: check meaning, agreement, verb links, register and task completion
steps.body: Editing is not only correcting accents. First check the task: did you answer every part, use the right register and stay within the official word range? Then check sentence meaning and reference; subject–verb and adjective agreement; verb government (avoir besoin de, s'intéresser à); relative forms; tense and mood triggers; and connectors. Read aloud to catch missing words and unclear rhythm. Correct errors that change meaning first, then refine vocabulary. Do not replace every simple phrase with a complicated one. A clear, accurate sentence is stronger than an elaborate sentence you cannot control.

steps.title: Final editing: check meaning, agreement, verb links, register and task completion
rows: La réponse compare les deux avis et formule une position.
The response compares both views and states a position.
Elle s'intéresse au programme dont nous avons parlé.
She is interested in the program we discussed.
Bien que le résultat soit utile, il reste limité.
Although the result is useful, it remains limited.
Cette mesure est coûteuse; son effet reste à évaluer.
This measure is costly; its effect remains to be assessed.

steps.prompt: What should you check first in a timed writing task?
options: Whether the conclusion introduces a new topic
Whether every sentence uses a rare word
Whether every part of the prompt is answered
steps.explain: Task completion comes before stylistic refinement.

steps.prompt: What should you do when a pronoun's reference is unclear?
steps.explain: Repeating a noun can restore a clear reference.

steps.prompt: What does a new transfer task measure?
options: Use of learning in an unfamiliar situation
Memory for a repeated script only
steps.explain: Transfer checks performance beyond rehearsed content.
